Chains don't show up in this verse. Luke 23:26 says the soldiers seized Simon of Cyrene, and "they put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus." Simon came in from the country and got handed something a whole lot heavier than a to-do list.
Spears aren't in this verse. Luke 23:26 says the soldiers seized Simon, and "they put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus." That's what lands on Simon, and he carries it behind Jesus.

Jesus doesn't name the leaders here. He's talking to the women, calling them "Daughters of Jerusalem," and He says to weep "for yourselves and for your children" (Luke 23:28). The ones He points them toward are themselves and their own little ones.

explanations.answer: One on His right and one on His left

explanations.answer: Both of them together on His right

explanations.answer: Forgive them because they don't know what they're doing
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing" (Luke 23:34). He's speaking while hanging on the cross. I think this is one of the lines people carry with them the longest.

explanations.answer: Judge them for everything they have done to Me
explanations.explanation: That's not what He asks. Luke 23:34 says, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." Forgive is the word He chooses, and He says it with all of this going on around Him.

explanations.answer: Take Me down from this cross before the night

explanations.answer: If You are the King of the Jews save Yourself
explanations.explanation: The soldiers say, "If You are the King of the Jews," and then, "save Yourself!" (Luke 23:37). They had already mocked Him and offered Him sour wine (Luke 23:36). The rulers were also talking about Him saving Himself (Luke 23:35).

explanations.answer: If You are a prophet tell us who hit You
explanations.explanation: Nothing about a prophet comes up in this scene. The soldiers say, "If You are the King of the Jews," and then, "save Yourself!" (Luke 23:37). Their mocking is about Him being a King and saving Himself.

explanations.answer: If You are the Son of God call down fire

explanations.answer: It is torn down the middle

explanations.answer: It is rolled up and hidden
explanations.explanation: Nothing gets rolled up or hidden. Luke 23:45 says the veil of the temple "was torn down the middle." It happens in the same verse where the sun is darkened.

explanations.answer: Into Your hands I commit My Spirit
explanations.explanation: Jesus calls out in a loud voice, "Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit" (Luke 23:46). He's speaking to His Father. After saying this, "He breathed His last."

explanations.answer: Send Your angels to take Me down
explanations.explanation: He doesn't ask for that. Luke 23:46 says Jesus called out in a loud voice, "Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit." Right after that, "He breathed His last."

explanations.answer: Let this darkness end right now
explanations.explanation: That's not what He says. The darkness is in Luke 23:44, but in Luke 23:46, Jesus calls out, "Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit." He speaks it in a loud voice, and then "He breathed His last."
